title: Don't trust the grade it implies
goal: Catch AI feedback that's generic, off-rubric, harsh, or mis-levelled — before it reaches a child.

blocks.title: It sounds fair — is it?
blocks.body:
AI feedback almost always *sounds* fair and professional. That's exactly why you check it.

Before any comment goes on a script, run four quick reads: does it match the rubric, is the level right for this child, is the tone kind, and is it fair? A confident comment can still be flat wrong.

blocks.question: Your rubric says a Level 4 answer "uses evidence to support each point." The AI wrote: "Excellent, well-argued work — clearly Level 4!" But the essay makes claims with no evidence at all. What do you do?

options.text: Keep it — the comment sounds confident and encouraging
Catch it — the praise doesn't match the rubric; rewrite it to name the missing evidence

blocks.explanation: Caught it. 👏 The comment praised something the rubric doesn't see in this work. Off-rubric praise feels kind but misleads the child. You read the criteria against the script — the AI only guessed.

blocks.question: For a struggling Class 6 student, the AI wrote: "This is careless and well below the expected standard. You clearly did not try." The facts may be right, but what's the problem?

options.text: Tone and level — it's harsh and demotivating for this child
Nothing — students need the hard truth

blocks.explanation: Right. It's not factually wrong — it's just unkind and pitched to crush, not lift. You know this child. Ask AI to keep it honest but warm, name one strength, and give one doable next step.

blocks.question: How ready do you feel to catch unfair or off-rubric AI feedback?
